title: Redefine table gesture model and automatic column-priority collapse
creator: Maya Chen
description: Unify the interaction model for table gestures (resize, reorder, column collapse, and multi-column selection) across density modes and virtualized render windows. Introduce an automatic column-priority collapse heuristic that preserves focused cells and frequently-accessed columns while reducing visual clutter on small viewports and high-density modes. Deliverables: updated interaction spec, annotated prototypes, accessibility matrix, telemetry plan, and handoff tokens for engineering.
acceptance_criteria: Single canonical gesture spec document that covers mouse, touch, and keyboard interactions for resize, reorder, and collapse across Compact/Cozy/Comfortable density modes
Prototype demonstrates kinetic resize with snap-to-priority and a fallback user grip when kernel/virtualization causes reflow jitter
Auto-collapse heuristic implemented as design tokens + config: priority ranking rules, minimum visible width, and focus-preservation policy
Accessibility: all interactions reachable via keyboard with clear ARIA announcements; screen reader testing notes attached
Telemetry events defined for resize start/end, collapse auto-trigger, manual override, and reflow fallback with suggested event names
Engineering handoff includes edge cases, sequence diagrams, and recommended debounce/batching values to avoid thrashing in virtualized lists
design_decisions: Favor predictability over aggressive compression: auto-collapse should never hide a column that contains the active cell or a pinned column
Introduce a three-tier priority score for columns: pinned, frequently-interacted (heat), content-density (chars-per-cell) — combined by weighted sum
Kinetic resize will expose a transient ghost-guide during drag which snaps to discrete breakpoints derived from tokenized min-widths
On touch devices, use longer hold to enable reorder mode to avoid accidental drags when scrolling virtualized lists
Density toggles adjust collapse thresholds and snap breakpoints; compact mode uses more aggressive thresholds but still respects focus-preservation
tradeoffs_considered: Complex heuristic vs. explicit user controls: opted for heuristic + clear manual override button (collapse chevron) to reduce UI clutter for >90% users
Performance vs. visible fidelity: ghost-guides add DOM paint cost but reduce user errors; guidance to engineering to render guides in overlay layer to avoid reflow
Telemetry volume: fine-grained events help debugging but risk noise; decided on sampling for high-frequency events (resize movements) and full capture for state transitions (collapse triggers)

Accessibility vs. gesture parity: some touch gestures are not possible to fully replicate on keyboard — provided alternative keyboard flows with clear announcements instead of identical gesture parity
implementation_notes: Provide a Token: table.column.priority.weights -> stringified weights for pinned/heat/density so server and client can align decisions
Suggested debounce for virtualization reflow: 120ms for continuous drag, 300ms for programmatic collapse to avoid layout thrash
Expose an opt-in flag on Table component: collapseHeuristic: 'auto' | 'conservative' | 'off'
Include a concise edge-case matrix: frozen columns, multi-select row mode, column with dynamic width (chips/badges), embedded interactive content
Add a small visual affordance for manual override (compact chevron) that persists for 6s after automatic collapse to teach users about the feature
